subject: Plan assembly + feature fallback options for Scoutly
messages:
From: Tom Rivera <tom.rivera@scoutly.com>
To: ben_carter@redwood.com
Cc: Procurement Ops <procurement@scoutly.com>
Date: 2027-08-09T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Questions on mixing tiers & fallback behavior for Scoutly

Hi Ben —

Thanks again for the demo last week. Procurement and engineering want to iron out how we’d assemble a plan that mixes Dedicated capacity for our realtime inference and Hosted for bursty workloads. A few specific asks:

- If we move a portion of traffic from Dedicated -> Hosted for an emergency, can we guarantee feature parity (function/tool calling, streaming) or will certain features be disabled?
- If Scoutly downgrades a tier mid-quarter, how are credits or unused Dedicated capacity handled?
- We have a strict requirement for a predictable failover: prefer region failover, then model-variant fallback, then temporary throttling. Can you show how that would work in an agreement?

Also attaching the draft SOW and the price sheet we pulled together — would appreciate a clear mapping to Redwood SKUs.

Cheers,
Tom
VP Product, Scoutly
From: ben_carter@redwood.com
To: Tom Rivera <tom.rivera@scoutly.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, laura_bennett@redwood.com
Date: 2027-08-09T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Questions on mixing tiers & fallback behavior for Scoutly

Tom —

Great questions — answered inline below and summarized with next steps. Attaching a plan matrix that maps Scoutly requirements to our SKUs.

1) Feature parity during emergency routing:
   - Hosted supports the same feature set as Dedicated for the exact model families we include in your catalog (generation, streaming, function calling). The only caveat is very large dedicated-only quantized variants: if your Dedicated pool uses a highly quantized model that we do not host in the shared cluster, we’ll route to the closest compatible hosted variant and keep function/tool calling intact.

2) Downgrade mid-quarter & unused Dedicated capacity:
   - Standard approach: pro-rated credit for unused committed hours for the remainder of the billing period, applied as account credits within 30 days of request.
   - For Reserved Dedicated with multi-month commits, we offer a one-time reallocation credit up to 20% toward Hosted consumption during the next billing cycle (subject to approval).

3) Failover ordering: region -> model-variant -> throttling.
   - We can codify this as a routing policy in the SOW and Console. If region failover triggers, we’ll attempt same-variant in failover region; if capacity not available, automatic fallback to the next certified variant in your model catalog.

Summary / next steps:
- I’ll update the SOW with routing policy language and the downgrade credit clause.
- Marissa, can you confirm the exact percentage reallocation credit we can offer for a 12‑month reserved commitment?
- Laura, can you confirm Hosted variant parity for the three model families Scoutly uses (gpt-openseq-13B, llama-lite-7B, rwd-embed-3B)?

Tom — are you available for a 30-minute call tomorrow at 10am PT to finalize the SOW language?

Best,
Ben
Enterprise Sales Lead
Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood_plan_matrix_v2.csv
From: marissa_cole@redwood.com
To: ben_carter@redwood.com, laura_bennett@redwood.com
Date: 2027-08-09T12:20:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Questions on mixing tiers & fallback behavior for Scoutly

Ben / Laura —

We can offer the 20% reallocation credit for a 12-month commit as proposed, but finance will push if they want more. If Scoutly signs up for a 24-month commit, we can move to 30% reallocation credit and an additional execution credit (one month of burst Hosted credits).

Note on downgrade mechanics (operational): credits are applied at the invoice level and can't be remapped to a different legal entity. We should make this explicit in the SOW.

I'll join the call with Tom and bring a pricing example.

—Marissa
From: laura_bennett@redwood.com
To: ben_carter@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com, Tom Rivera <tom.rivera@scoutly.com>
Date: 2027-08-09T14:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Questions on mixing tiers & fallback behavior for Scoutly

Tom —

Quick technical confirmation: Hosted supports function/tool calling, streaming, and structured outputs for the model families listed. For gpt-openseq-13B and rwd-embed-3B we have 1:1 parity. For llama-lite-7B we have a hosted variant that is 8-bit quantized; function calling is supported, but you may see ~5-8% change in tail latency under peak. We can add explicit variant-selection policy to the catalog so your engineers can pin behavior.

Also note: when fallback to a different variant occurs, we add a header in the response (x-redwood-fallback: variant-id) and emit a trace in Console to help you correlate.

Laura
Staff Engineer, Runtime
From: Tom Rivera <tom.rivera@scoutly.com>
To: ben_carter@redwood.com
Cc: Procurement Ops <procurement@scoutly.com>, laura_bennett@redwood.com
Date: 2027-08-10T08:46:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Questions on mixing tiers & fallback behavior for Scoutly

Ben / Laura —

Thanks, that helps a lot. We need the SOW language for:
- explicit downgrade credit formula and timing,
- routing policy with the three-step failover and a maximum allowed latency bump (5% preferred),
- confirmation of the header/trace behavior so our observability team can map it.

Call tomorrow 10am PT works for me. I’ve forwarded an internal procurement checklist — I’ll bring the checklist and our procurement lead to the call.

Thanks,
Tom
From: ben_carter@redwood.com
To: Tom Rivera <tom.rivera@scoutly.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, laura_bennett@redwood.com
Date: 2027-08-11T16:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Questions on mixing tiers & fallback behavior for Scoutly

Tom —

Good call today. Recap and immediate deliverables:

1) SOW draft: I’ll push a tracked SOW with the downgrade credit formula (pro-rate remaining committed hours + 20% reallocation credit for 12m, 30% for 24m) and the clause that credits apply at invoice level.

2) Routing policy language: region -> model-variant -> throttling with a target max latency increase of 7% (legal/ops won’t accept 5% as a strict SLA; we agreed to 7% as a measurable target, with monthly quality review).

3) Observability: Laura will add the x-redwood-fallback header and Console trace details; we’ll include a small integration note for Scoutly’s observability team.

I’ve attached the plan matrix and SOW draft to the email thread for your review. If you can confirm by Friday EOD, we’ll get this into legal for signature next week.

Ben
Enterprise Sales Lead, Redwood Inference

Attachments: Scoutly_SOW_draft.pdf, redwood_plan_matrix_v2.csv
